ambiguities_declared: P[17]-P[23] (input designators 3-9, covering pressure zones, 12-inch and larger pipes, 8-inch pipes connecting zones, 6-inch pipes to remote areas, storage facilities, pump stations, and control valves) are flagged in the source as logical-anchor-ambiguity review items with no confirmed (a)(2)(i)(B)(3)-(9) labels; content is clear but sub-numbering was not guessed.

The monitoring-locations/samples table (TABLE[1]) has 17 rows spanning both Subpart H and Ground Water systems across many population size categories; only two representative rows (Subpart H <500 and Ground Water ≥500,000) were extracted as claims. Remaining rows would need a dedicated extraction pass for full table-cell coverage.

P[10] (141.602(a)(1)(ii)(E)) ties existing-monitoring-plan retention to 'paragraph (b)(5) of this section,' but current (b) lettering has retention appearing in (b)(7), not (b)(5); by contrast P[33] (141.602(a)(2)(ii)(H)) correctly cites (b)(7) for the same type of retention obligation. This cross-reference inconsistency was preserved verbatim rather than resolved.

Several technical/design requirements (pipe-coverage percentages, model calibration deadlines, IDSE report retention duration) do not map cleanly onto the controlled relation vocabulary (has-mcl/mclg/mrdl/mrdlg, requires-monitoring, compliance-basis, applies-to, defined-as, requires-treatment-technique); nearest-fit relations were assigned (requires-monitoring or compliance-basis) and should be reviewed for accuracy.

verified_quotes.exact_text: Your system specific study plan must be based on either existing monitoring results as required under paragraph (a)(1) of this section or modeling as required under paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
Samples must be collected no earlier than five years prior to the study plan submission date.
Each location must be sampled once during the peak historical month for TTHM levels or HAA5 levels or the month of warmest water temperature for every 12 months of data submitted for that location.
All required calibration must be completed no later than 12 months after plan submission.
Description of how all requirements will be completed no later than 12 months after you submit your system specific study plan.
You must retain a complete copy of your IDSE report submitted under this section for 10 years after the date that you submitted your IDSE report.
The model must simulate 24 hour variation in demand and show a consistently repeating 24 hour pattern of residence time.
If you fail to correct deficiencies or respond to inquiries to the State's satisfaction, you must conduct standard monitoring under § 141.601.
You must recommend and justify subpart V compliance monitoring locations and timing based on the protocol in § 141.605.
TTHM and HAA5 results must be based on samples collected and analyzed in accordance with § 141.131.
